text: Nominalism [Lat. nominalis , from nomen , a name]: Ger. Nominalismus ; Fr. nominalisme ; Ital. nominalismo . The doctrine that universals have no objective existence or validity; in its extreme form, that they are only names ( nomina , flatus vocis ), that is, creations of language for purposes of convenient communication. See REALISM (1) for full account and history. ( J.D. )
